clue.text: Working capital advances male film star

indicators.note: advances says the male letter moves forward, here right to the front of the string

parts.note: a machine that is working is on
Rome is the Italian capital

explanation.surface: A busy capital city promotes a male film star.
explanation.walkthrough: ON and ROME give ONROME; 'advances' moves the M to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Marilyn Monroe was one of Hollywood's most famous screen actresses.

clue.text: Haggard heroine among users, deployed as female escort

indicators.note: among puts the heroine within the reworked letters
deployed means the letters of users are spread out into a new order

parts.note: She is the title figure of H. Rider Haggard's novel She

explanation.surface: A novel's heroine is sent out among the users as a woman who shows people to their seats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deployed' makes URESS for 'among' to hold. 'Haggard' is H. Rider Haggard, the author, not a description of a weary heroine.
explanation.definitionFit: An usheress is a woman usher, one who escorts people to their seats in a theatre or church.

clue.text: The most brutish thug heading off to stop all others

indicators.note: to stop means to plug a gap, so the shortened thug sits inside

parts.note: the rest means all the others

indicators.note: heading off says the first letter of the word for thug is dropped

parts.note: a rough is a violent hooligan

explanation.surface: The most violent thug sets off to block everyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' leaves OUGH, which 'to stop' plugs into the word for all others.
explanation.definitionFit: Roughest is the superlative of rough, meaning most coarse and violent.

clue.text: Almost messing up breadcake

indicators.note: almost says the word falls one letter short of complete, losing its final letter

parts.note: to muff something is to bungle it, so messing up is muffing

explanation.surface: Someone nearly ruins a bun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' cuts the last letter G from MUFFING.
explanation.definitionFit: A muffin is a flat round bread roll, the kind toasted and buttered for tea.

clue.text: Raising pitiful bum after I left

indicators.note: bum as an adjective means poor or broken, so the letters are knocked out of order
left means the letter I has gone away from the word pitiful

explanation.surface: Someone lifts a sorry backside once they have gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' takes one I out of PITIFUL, leaving PTIFUL, which 'bum' rearranges. 'bum' looks like a noun for a backside.
explanation.definitionFit: An uplift is a raising up, as of land or of spirits.

clue.text: By rolling up part of joint, incur disgrace

indicators.note: in a down entry rolling up reads the word for by from bottom to top

parts.note: per means by, as in per post
a roach is the butt end of a cannabis joint

explanation.surface: Rolling a spliff gets someone into trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'rolling up' gives REP. 'incur' is only a link here; the noun sense of disgrace is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A reproach can mean a source of shame or discredit, as in being a reproach to the family.

clue.text: Author's position about play

definitions.note: read as author is, the apostrophe-s linking the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: about signals turning the word for position round

parts.note: a slot is a position, as in a time slot
to toy is to play idly

explanation.surface: A writer's stance on a stage play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' gives TOLS; the 's after Author is read as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Leo Tolstoy was the Russian novelist who wrote War and Peace.

clue.text: Leap by black fighter

parts.note: a jump is a leap
jet means deep glossy black

explanation.surface: A leap made by a black boxer.
explanation.definitionFit: A jump jet is a vertical take-off warplane such as the Harrier, so a fighter aircraft.

clue.text: Extremely lithe mesomorph moving around on this?

definitions.text: Extremely lithe mesomorph moving around on this?

indicators.note: moving around says the letters shift into a new order
extremely takes only the outermost letters of lithe

explanation.surface: A supple, muscular gymnast swings around on a piece of apparatus.
explanation.walkthrough: The ends of 'lithe' give LE; with MESOMORPH that is shuffled. The whole clue also describes the answer: a mesomorph is a muscular body type.
explanation.definitionFit: A gymnast performing on this vaulting apparatus swings around above its handles, so the clue pictures its use.

clue.text: Grieg opera superficially composed around piano chord

indicators.note: around says the rearranged letters surround the piano symbol
composed means the letters are arranged afresh, as music is written
superficially means only the surface of the word, its outside letters

parts.note: p is the musical marking for piano, soft

explanation.surface: A Norwegian composer's opera written around a piano chord.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' makes AREGGIO, which 'around' wraps about the piano letter. Grieg wrote no opera, which makes the surface a trap.
explanation.definitionFit: An arpeggio is a broken chord, its notes played one after another rather than together.

clue.text: Monk et al. force prickly shrubs to be dead-headed

parts.note: F is the physics symbol for force

indicators.note: dead-headed, like a pruned flower, means losing the top letter

parts.note: briars are thorny bushes

explanation.surface: A setter called Monk and friends make thorny bushes lose their spent flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dead-headed' drops the B from BRIARS. Monk is also the setter's pseudonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Friars are members of religious orders, close kin to monks, so a monk and others like him.

clue.text: Paul's men touring continually

definitions.note: the surname belonging to Paul, the American patriot

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the soldiers surround the word for always

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, are soldiers, so men
ever means always or continually

explanation.surface: Paul's soldiers are always on tour.
explanation.walkthrough: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a British army corps, so soldiers or men.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Revere was the American silversmith famous for his midnight ride in 1775.

clue.text: Mo scoffing back first-class trifles

indicators.note: scoffing means eating up, so the moment swallows the other letters

parts.note: mo is short for moment, a minute

indicators.note: back says the first-class letters are reversed

parts.note: A1 is first-class, written as the letters AI

explanation.surface: Mo wolfs down top-quality little desserts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' gives IA for 'scoffing'. 'trifles' looks like puddings but means small matters.
explanation.definitionFit: Minutiae are small, trivial details, which is what trifles also means.

clue.text: Former president getting paper's gossip

parts.note: Bush was the surname of two US presidents
the Telegraph is a British daily newspaper

explanation.surface: An ex-president is getting tittle-tattle from a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: The bush telegraph is informal word-of-mouth spreading of news, rumour and gossip.

clue.text: Rank secured by Black and Tan boss

indicators.note: secured by means held in place by the other two pieces around it

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
to tan is to beat, as in tanning someone's hide
a rank is a row, as in a rank of soldiers

explanation.surface: A rank is held by an officer of the Black and Tans.
explanation.walkthrough: The Black and Tans were a notorious British auxiliary force in Ireland in 1920-21, which the surface evokes.
explanation.definitionFit: To browbeat is to bully or intimidate, much as to boss someone about.

clue.text: Travel as boxing promoters should do?

definitions.meaning: to move around from place to place
promoters of boxing are meant to arrange a fight, a bout

explanation.walkthrough: Read as three words, it is what a boxing promoter does: obtains a bout.
explanation.definitionFit: To get about is to move from place to place, to travel; read literally it means arranging a fight.

clue.text: Adult and child netting easy goal if necessary

indicators.note: netting means catching in a net, so the two letters surround the goal

parts.note: A is the film classification for adult
a tap-in is a simple goal from very close range

explanation.surface: A grown-up and youngster score a simple goal when needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'netting' looks like scoring, but it is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: At a pinch means if really necessary, at a push.

clue.text: Also sign to enter party — cheers

parts.note: too means also

indicators.note: to enter means the zodiac sign goes inside the party

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration
Leo is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A star sign also gets in to a party, and everyone raises a glass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cheers' is the British informal goodbye here, not a toast.
explanation.definitionFit: Toodle-oo is a jaunty British goodbye, and cheers is used in Britain as a casual farewell too.

clue.text: Want to contribute to avante-garde art history

indicators.note: contribute to means these letters make up part of the following words

explanation.surface: Someone wants to add to the history of avant-garde art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Want' looks like a verb but is the noun, a lack.
explanation.definitionFit: A dearth is a scarcity or lack, the sense of want as need.

clue.text: Last exposure and future picture do this

parts.words: exposure and future picture do this
parts.note: each of these three words finishes with the same three letters, U R E, so they end in that letter group

explanation.surface: A long photographic exposure and a picture yet to come must hold out.
explanation.walkthrough: Exposure, future and picture each finish in URE, so they END URE.
explanation.definitionFit: To last is to persist or survive, the same as to endure.

clue.text: Ignoring ruin, reputation damaged in China?

indicators.note: damaged means the letters of reputation are broken up and reassembled

parts.note: taken as written, the anagram's whole pool
these letters are what Ignoring leaves out of the pool

explanation.surface: Setting aside ruin, someone's good name is harmed in China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ignoring ruin' takes R, U, I, N out of REPUTATION and 'damaged' rearranges what is left. The question mark marks China as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A teapot is often made of china porcelain, so it is an example of china ware.

clue.text: Blunt object with section cut near end

indicators.note: near means placed right beside the next piece
a section cut out means a chunk from the middle of the word is removed, leaving its ends

parts.note: an object is a thing, taken here as the word itself
an end is a purpose or use, as in to what end

explanation.surface: A blunt instrument with a slice cut off close to its tip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with section cut' removes the middle run JEC, leaving OBT. 'Blunt object' reads as one weapon, but 'Blunt' alone is the definition. 'end' meaning use, as in to no end, is a loose equivalence.
explanation.definitionFit: Obtuse means not sharp or pointed, so dull-edged, and figuratively slow-witted.

clue.text: Alongside current that has run eastwards

indicators.note: in an across entry eastwards means moving to the right, so the run letter shifts along

parts.note: abroad means widely current, as a rumour is abroad
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Beside a sea current flowing east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eastwards' moves the R of ABROAD two places right.
explanation.definitionFit: Aboard can mean alongside, as in a ship lying aboard another.

clue.text: Briefly covers first son's remains

parts.note: subs, short for substitutes, cover for others
1st, written IST, is first

explanation.surface: Briefly protects the eldest son's remains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remains' looks like a noun but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To subsist is to continue to exist, or remain.

clue.text: Transport runs by unopened land

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: unopened means losing the first letter

parts.note: to land a fish or prize is to capture it

explanation.surface: A vehicle hurries past closed-off countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transport' is the noun of delight; 'land' is the verb, as in landing a catch, without its C.
explanation.definitionFit: Transport can mean ecstasy, a state of overwhelming joy, just as rapture does.

clue.text: Teachers examine crank

parts.note: the NUT was the National Union of Teachers, a British trade union
to case a place is to examine it before a burglary

explanation.surface: Teachers inspect a piece of machinery.
explanation.walkthrough: The NUT was Britain's National Union of Teachers.
explanation.definitionFit: A crank is an eccentric person, a nutter or madman.
